title: Can Ad Hoc Service Count Toward Your Seniority?
desc: The Supreme Court ruled on 29 July 2026 that Uttarakhand Deputy Collectors can count ad hoc service towards seniority when the State caused the delay.
why: A Supreme Court ruling in a case from Uttarakhand answers a question many government employees face: does officiating or ad hoc service count towards seniority when regular promotion is delayed by the department itself?
keyPoints: The Supreme Court held that ad hoc service counts towards seniority when the delay in regular promotion is the state's own fault.
Uttarakhand Deputy Collectors promoted on an ad hoc basis in 2007 got seniority from 1 October 2007, not a later date.
Skipping the Public Service Commission's consultation did not cancel the promotions, since that rule was held to be directory.
The State must issue a revised seniority list within three months of the judgment.

sections.h: What did the Supreme Court decide about ad hoc service in Uttarakhand?
p: On 29 July 2026, the Supreme Court held in State of Uttarakhand v. Jagdish Chandra Kandpal that Deputy Collectors promoted on an ad hoc basis in Uttarakhand in 2007 could count that officiating service towards seniority under the proviso to Rule 24(4) of the state's service rules. It fixed their regular seniority from 1 October 2007, not a later date.

The Court also said the State could not take advantage of its own continuing default. Officials had failed to consult the Uttarakhand Public Service Commission before the 2007 promotions, but the judges treated that consultation requirement as directory, not mandatory, since the lapse was the department's fault, not the employees'.

sections.h: Does this help other Uttarakhand government employees too?
p: The judgment is specific to Deputy Collectors promoted within the promotee quota in 2007, so it does not automatically cover every service dispute. But the principle behind it — that officiating or ad hoc service counts towards seniority when the delay was caused by the department, not the employee — is one that other Uttarakhand employees can raise in similar seniority or promotion disputes.

The Court also went further than the 2019 High Court order, which had only asked the State to re-check vacancies. It directed the State to issue a revised seniority list within three months, instead of sending the matter back for fresh verification.

whatToDo: Check your appointment order for the exact date your officiating or ad hoc service began.
Ask your department in writing, or file an RTI request, for the current seniority list and the vacancy position in your promotee quota.
If a sanctioned vacancy existed before your regular promotion and the delay was the department's fault, put this in a written representation to your department.
If the department does not respond, a seniority or promotion dispute can be taken to the Central Administrative Tribunal (CAT) or the High Court of Uttarakhand, depending on the post.

hi.title: क्या तदर्थ (एड हॉक) सेवा वरिष्ठता में गिनी जाएगी?
keyPoints: सुप्रीम कोर्ट ने कहा कि नियमित पदोन्नति में देरी अगर राज्य की अपनी गलती से हुई हो, तो तदर्थ सेवा वरिष्ठता में गिनी जाएगी।
2007 में तदर्थ आधार पर पदोन्नत उत्तराखंड डिप्टी कलेक्टरों को वरिष्ठता 1 अक्टूबर 2007 से मिलेगी।
लोक सेवा आयोग से सलाह न लेने से पदोन्नति रद्द नहीं हुई, क्योंकि यह नियम अनिवार्य नहीं माना गया।
राज्य सरकार को तीन महीने के भीतर संशोधित वरिष्ठता सूची जारी करनी होगी।
